# Recursive containers and handle-array storage (SIM-006)

The task module runs every positive fixture through the public CLI in both HDL
optimizer modes on legacy, compact/portable and compact/GMP values. The feature fixtures without runtime warnings
also run after the frontend snapshot and owned Db are destroyed; the two
fixtures that warn also check their exact runtime stderr. Expected outputs are
derived by hand from the cited clauses, not captured from llg.

Containers are values (SV 7.5-7.10): assignment, formals and results copy the
container and its elements. Handle elements (class objects, events,
processes, semaphores, mailboxes, virtual interfaces, chandles) copy the
handle only, never the designated object.

| Fixture | Clause and independent oracle |
| --- | --- |
| `subroutine_containers` | IEEE 1800-2009 §§7.5, 7.8, 7.10, 13.3-13.5. `pop_all` drains its own copy: `abc`, caller still has 3. `grow` keeps 1.5 2.5 through `new[4](old)` and fills 2*0.5, 3*0.5: `4 2.5 1.0 1.5`. `touch` adds 100 through copied handles (objects 1, 2 become 101, 102) and clears only its copy (caller size 2). `evens(7)` = {0,2,4,6}: size 4, element 3 = 6; `void'(evens(3))` discards a result. Recursive `depth(4, dummy)` pushes 4..0 into per-activation copies: 5, caller still empty. Static `counter` keeps its local queue: 1 then 2. `keys` sums value*key length: 2*2+3*3 = 13. `recs` appends {z,2.5} and edits element 0 in place: 2, `y!`, `z`, 2.5. `fill` outputs {a,b}; `bump` turns {1,2} into {7,2,2}; `sum('{4,5})` builds its argument at the call: 9. Task `slow` copies {1,2,3}, waits 1 ns, appends 10: 16 at time 1. |
| `record_column_results` | §§7.2, 7.5, 7.10, 13.4 with RTL-101 column-layout records (member array of 5,000 cells). `cols` returns {`x.a[4999]`, `x.t`, `z.t`, `extra.size()`} = {5, 3, 40, 2}, copies `x` into `y` with `y.a[1] = 77` (so `o.a[4999]` is 5) and increments the inout `z.t` to 41. The discarded `void'(cols(...))` increments it again to 42 and leaves `b` at 4 entries. `ins(r, 2)` returns `a[0] + t`, `a[1] + t` = 13, 23. `rr` returns the real array {7 * 0.5, 2.5} = {3.5, 2.5} and `o.t` = 8; discarding it with `r.t = 9` sets `o.t` to 10 and leaves `v[0]` at 3.5. |
| `procedural_containers` | §§6.21, 7.5, 7.10, 23.2.2. Block locals: queue {3}, strings `w x` after `push_front`, real 2.5. The loop's `automatic` queue restarts empty each iteration: size 1 holding 2 on the last pass. The task's `static` queue keeps both visits (2) while its automatic local holds one (1). Port `qin`/`sout` containers follow the driver: `v1 v2`, then `v3`. |
| `class_containers` | §§8.5, 8.9, 8.13, 7.5-7.10. Each object owns its instance containers: `k` gets 3, 4 and, through the alias `alias_k`, 1 (total 8); `k2` has 9. The static `shared` queue collects every `add` from every object: 30 40 90 10 50, so 5 entries with `shared[4]` = 50. A derived object reaches the inherited queue and table: `more` adds 5, then `q[0] + 100` = 105; one key; its own real array holds 1.5. `drop_front` pops 3 then deletes the rest of `k.q` (total 0) without touching `k2` (9). |
| `nested_containers` | §§7.5, 7.10, 10.10. Queue of queues: `push_back({1,2})`, `push_back({3})`, `push_front('{4,5,6})`, `insert(1, {})`, then a copy of dynamic array {7,8} (the later write of 70 to the source is not seen) and `q[1] = {9,9,9,9}`: 5 elements with sizes 3 4 2 1 2, `q[4][0]` = 7, `q[0][2]` = 6. Dynamic array of dynamic arrays: `new[3]` row (element 2 reads 0) and pattern row {5,6}. Queues of strings and an int-keyed table of queues: `x`, `z`, 2; 3 entries under key 10, `a[-1][1]` = 2, 2 keys. Summing nested `size()` over the outer queue: 3+4+2+1+2 = 12. |
| `record_elements` | §§7.2, 7.4, 7.5, 7.8, 7.10. Queue after `push_back(first)`, `push_front(second)`, `insert(1, second)`: second second first. Runtime-indexed member writes change only `q[2]`: 99, 5, `first!`, inner 3; `q[0].arr[1]` is 21. `y = q[2]` is a deep copy (renaming `q[2]` leaves `first!`). Writes through missing keys create entries from the defaults: `keyed`, 1 entry, `created`, exists, `arr[0]` 0. `pop_back` returns `changed` with r 2.50, leaving 2; `delete(0)` leaves `second`. `new[3](d)` keeps both elements and adds a default (empty name), r 4.25 written afterwards, inner 3. `delete()` empties both. |
| `handle_arrays` | §§7.4, 8.4, 9.7, 15.3, 15.4, 25.9. Virtual interfaces in a range `[2:3]` array and a queue designate the interface: writing 21 through `vq[0]` is seen by `i1` and `vifs[3]`. Copying class-handle arrays shares objects: 50 through `copy[1]`, 60 through `cq[0]`, `copy[2] == objs[2]`. Semaphores with 1 and 2 keys grant `try_get(1)`/`try_get(2)`. Two queue entries name one mailbox: 7 put through one is received through the other. At 2 ns the first forked process waits and the second has finished; `kill` makes it KILLED. |
| `event_containers` | §§6.17, 7.4.5, 7.5, 7.8.6, 7.10, 15.5. Queue {e3,null,e1,e2}: size 4, one null; element 2 is `e1`. After `delete(1)` element 1 is still `e1`; `pop_front` returns `e3`. Missing associative entries read as null (with the §7.8.6 warning) and `exists(5)` is 1. `new[2]` creates two distinct events (Table 6-7 default for event elements); after `d[1] = d[0]` both name one event, so `->d[0]` at 1 ns wakes `@(d[1])`, and `->q[0]` (e1) at 2 ns makes `q[0].triggered` true. `new[3](d)` keeps the sharing and adds a new event. `reverse` gives {e2,e1}. 64 pushes with `e2` at 40 plus `push_front(e1)` force reallocation: 65 entries, index 41 is `e2`, 63 nulls. `fire_all` triggers its copy's non-null entries at 3 ns, waking both waiters. `q = {}` empties the queue and a read past the end is null. |
| `assoc_defaults` | §7.8.6, Table 7-1, §7.9.11. Missing `a[7]` reads 0 and `s["nope"]` the empty string, each with a warning. The index `4'bx01x` is invalid: the read warns and yields 0, the write warns and is ignored (still 1 entry). Wildcard `w[6]` is missing: `xx`. With `'{default: 42}` a missing key reads 42 silently and creates nothing. A missing real reads 0.0 with a warning. `cnt["k"] += 2` reads the default 0 (warning) and creates 2; `++` makes 3; `a[1]--` gives 4. |
| `dynamic_events`, `queue_events`, `associative_events`, `process_array`, `process_formal`, `semaphore_array`, `mailbox_array`, `virtual_associative`, `dynamic_call` | Adopted FND-002 witnesses (ledger L-F02-11-01, L-F12-02-04, L-F12-05-01, L-F12-05-02, L-F12-06-01, L-F12-07-01 and the SIM-003 `dynamic_call` item); each expected line is the witness's `Expected:` header; the copies end with a quiet `$finish(0)`. |

## Negatives

| Fixture | Boundary |
| --- | --- |
| `neg_class_key_builtin` | A class key of a built-in class (`semaphore`, `mailbox`, `process`) rejects at the declaration. |
| `neg_nested_key_type` | A nested key type without runtime support rejects at the declaration, not at the first use. |
| `neg_class_key_item_index` | `item.index` of a class-keyed array needs a handle iterator index, which has no form yet. |
| `container_initializers` | §§6.21, 7.5.1, 10.5. `d` is `new[n]` after `n` = 3; `q2` copies `q1` ('{4, 5}): `q2[1]` = 5; `e` = `new[4](d2)` keeps 7, 8 then defaults: size 4, `e[1]` = 8; `c` = {4, 5, 6}: `c[2]` = 6; `k` reads both containers after their initializers: 3 + 2 = 5; `f(2)`: `t` has 2 elements and `u[2]` = 2: 4. |
| `neg_wildcard_foreach`, `neg_wildcard_first`, `neg_wildcard_find` | §7.8.1: a wildcard-index associative array cannot be traversed by `foreach` or used with methods that return an index (frontend diagnostics). |
| `queue_concatenation` | §§7.10.4, 10.10. `{1, 2, 3}` then `{q[1:$], 0}` gives 2 3 0; `{q[0] + 10, q}` reads `q[0]` before the write: 12 2 3 0; strings `{s, "b", s}` give a b a; reals append 2.5; record elements copy by value (`rq[1].k` = 5, the appended copy keeps 1, name x); the bounded queue `[$:2]` keeps 3 of 4 elements (with the runtime warning on stderr); the automatic local `t` doubles to 4 5 4 5 (4 + 5 = 9); a dynamic array takes element values (3 elements, last 9). |
| `neg_dynamic_array_concat` | Legal by §10.10; an array item in a concatenation assigned to a dynamic array is rejected explicitly (queue targets combine array items). |
| `nested_element_methods` | §§7.4.5, 7.8, 7.8.6, 7.10.2, 7.10.5, 7.12 (quotes below). Methods, whole reads and whole writes of a queue or dynamic array nested in an element of a queue, dynamic array or integral- or string-keyed associative array change or read that element in place. Queue of queues `{5}`, `{1,2}`, `{1,2}` after `push_front`/`insert`; `qq[0].push_back(6)`, `qq[1].push_front(0)`, `qq[2].insert(1, 7)`, `qq[2][0] = 11`: `5 6`, `0 1 2`, `11 7 2`; `delete(0)` and `delete()`: `1 2` and size 0. `push_back(qq[0][0] + qq[0].size())` reads before the push: 5 + 2 = 7; `reverse` 7 6 5, `sort` 5 6 7; `pop_front` 5, then `sum` 13, `product` 42, `find` > 6 is `7`; `qq.push_back(qq[0])` copies `6 7`. Dynamic array of queues: `1 22` and `3`. `aq[7].push_front(1)` and `aq[k].push_back(k)` create entries 7 and 3 (three entries); `aq[3]` = `3 1` (the second push reads size 1). String-keyed: `sq["a"]` = `1 2 4 1` (the pushed `sq["b"].size()` is 1), `$size(sq["b"])` = 1; `sd["k"] = new[4]` and `sd["j"] = d`: 2 entries, sizes 4 and 3, `sd["j"]` reads back `0 0 9`; `sq["none"].size()` reads 0 without creating an entry (still 2). Queue of dynamic arrays after push/insert, `qd[1][0] = 66`, `qd[0].delete()`: 3 0 66 9. The bounded `[$:1]` element keeps `7 1` and discards the third push with a warning (stderr). Three levels: 2 2 2 9; strings `w x y`; records `2 y`, `1 x` after `push_front`, the copied-in record removed by `delete()`. |
| `nested_element_arguments` | §13.5.1 L19086-19087: "Pass by value is the default mechanism for passing arguments to subroutines. This argument passing mechanism works by copying each argument into the subroutine area." A queue or dynamic array nested in an element of a queue, dynamic array or integral- or string-keyed associative array is copied whole into an input container formal of a function (in an assignment, a `$display` argument, a method argument) or a task: `total('{1,2,3}) + total('{5,6})` = 17; `total('{4})` = 4, `dsum('{7,8})` = 15; the task receives `aq[3]` = `'{9}` and `total(sq["k"])` = 21; an index computed from `x` (17 - 17 = 0) gives 6; `qq[1].push_back(total(qq[0]))` appends 6 to `'{4}` (size 2, total 10). Matches industry-standard behaviour in both optimizer modes. |
| `computed_handle_containers` | §§8.4, 7.10.2, 11.3.5, 12.7.3. A property container selected through an element select or a call (`list[k].q`, `am[3].m`, `pick(1).q`) names the object the handle designates at that evaluation. §8.4 L9653: "Accessing nonstatic members (see 8.8) or virtual methods (see 8.19) via a null object handle is illegal.", so the guarded `k > 5 && list[k + 7].q.size() > 0` and the skipped arm of `?:` must not evaluate their handle: `calls` stays 0, then 1, then 2.. |
| `class_container_forms` | §§7.9.4-7.9.7 (traversal methods update their `ref` index; the index may be any variable of the index type), 8.6 (`this` names the object's properties). A class may declare `first`/`next` without becoming an enum method. Matches industry-standard behaviour. |
| `call_result_selects` | §§7.10.2, 8.4, 13.4.1. A container result is a value: `make(4).size()` is 4, `amap().exists("y")` is 0, `c.m().size()` is 1. A select on a call (`make(3)[1]` = 2, `names()[1]` = `b`, `amap()["x"]` = 3) is outside the 1800-2009 primary grammar but the frontend admits it; the values are derived by hand. Each call runs once per evaluation: `n` counts them. `f2[5] = 3` writes the implicit result variable (§13.4.1). |
| `call_container_operands` | §§11.3.5 L14430-14435, 13.5.1. An actual that is not a variable (`q[1:2]`, `twice(q)`, `words()`, `{q, 4}`, `qq[0]`) is built where the call is evaluated, in any expression. "When short circuiting occurs, any side effects or runtime errors that would have occurred due to evaluation of the short circuited operand expression shall not occur.": `q.size() > 100 && sum(twice(q)) > 0` does not call `twice`, so `n` is 3. Some simulators build the actual early; llg follows the clause. Other lines match industry-standard behaviour. |
| `neg_computed_handle_wait` | Legal by §9.4.3; a wait re-evaluates its condition after the statement's handle local is gone, so a computed receiver in it is rejected explicitly. |
| `neg_computed_handle_assoc_foreach` | A `foreach` array that calls a subroutine is outside the §12.7.3 grammar; a keyed or nested traversal would have to call again at each bound check and is rejected explicitly. |
| `nested_element_expressions` | §§7.4.5, 7.8, 7.10.2, 13.5.2. `if (q[0].pop_front() == 1)` changes the element inside a condition; `return q[i].sum()`; `wr(q[0])` and `io(q[1])` write the element through the formal; `sq["a"][1] = 3` selects inside a string-keyed element; `sq["b"].push_back(sq["a"].pop_front())` changes two elements of one container with constant distinct keys. Matches industry-standard behaviour. |
| `nested_lazy_called_selector` | §11.3.5 L14430-14435: a skipped operand is not evaluated. A selector call of a nested associative array in the second operand of `&&`, `\|\|` or `?:` runs only when that operand does, also when the whole statement stages elements. |
| `neg_class_property_element_nba` | §6.21 L7007-7008: class properties are not written with nonblocking assignments, also through an element (decision S14-D5). |
| `neg_nested_two_changes` | Legal; a statement that changes two nested elements of one container whose selectors are not provably distinct (`sq[a].push_back(sq[b].pop_front())`) is rejected explicitly: each element is changed through a staged copy, and equal selectors would lose a change. |
| `nested_associative`, `nested_associative_forms`, `nested_associative_deep` | §7.4.5 L8122: "A multidimensional array is an array of arrays."; §7.8 L8587: "Associative arrays do not have any storage allocated until it is used". An associative array is an element like any other: nested in an associative array, queue or dynamic array it takes selects, methods, whole reads and writes, patterns, `foreach`, and `input` and `ref` actuals, and a class method returns the handles it holds (`streams[a][b]`). A missing outer key reads as empty and creates nothing. Matches industry-standard behaviour. |
| `nested_foreach` | §12.7.3 L18209: "Loop variables may be omitted to indicate no iteration over that dimension of the array"; L18185: "Each loop variable corresponds to one of the dimensions of the array." Fixed inner dimensions, associative outer dimensions and omitted slots. `foreach (w[, j])` runs the inner loop once, not once per row. Matches industry-standard behaviour. |
| `record_element_compound`, `record_field_compound` | §11.4.1. Compound writes and increments of members of record elements of queues, dynamic and associative arrays, fixed arrays and class properties; a missing associative key reads its default first. Matches industry-standard behaviour. |
| `semaphore_try_get_statement` | §15.3.4 L20422: "The semaphore try_get() method is used to procure a specified number of keys from a semaphore, but without blocking."; the result may be discarded with `void'`. Hand-derived: two of two keys taken, the third try returns 0; after one `put` the try returns 1. |
| `static_block_event` | §9.4.2. A static local of a procedural block is a variable `@` can wait on from a fork branch. Matches industry-standard behaviour. |
| `nested_ref_actuals` | §13.5.2 L19103: "Arguments passed by reference are not copied into the subroutine area, rather, a reference to the original argument is passed to the subroutine." A `ref` actual may be a class property through any handle or a record member. Matches industry-standard behaviour. |
| `neg_nested_task_ref`, `neg_nested_function_ref`, `neg_nested_keyed_function_ref` | Legal by §13.5.2; a nested queue or dynamic array has only a staged copy, which a reference must not alias, for a task or a function, `const` or not: rejected explicitly at the actual. |
| `class_keys_storage`, `class_keys_nested`, `class_keys_refs`, `class_keys_patterns`, `class_keys_gc` | Expected outputs checked against an independent simulator, all keys of one class. 7.8.3 L8682-8683: "A null index is valid." "The ordering is deterministic but arbitrary." 7.8.3 L8680-8681: "Indices can be objects of that particular type or derived from that type." Element types, record elements, class properties, parameterized statics, keys at every nesting level, `ref` elements, default and `null` key patterns, conditional merges. `class_keys_gc` also runs under `LLG_GC_STRESS=1 LLG_GC_VERIFY=1` and `LLG_GC_THRESHOLD=1`: objects only a key names, in globals, locals, class properties and nested arrays, survive. |
| `nested_write_arms` | Decision S07-D8; 10.4.1 L13025-13026 leaves the order undefined. Expected outputs checked against an independent simulator. A record conditional keeps the write when the taken arm's call deletes the entry and creates nothing when the arm is skipped; a queue element past the end of a queue the call deleted is an invalid index, so the write does nothing (7.4.6 L8235-8238); a callee's change to the array an input actual was read from stays. |
| `nested_write_lost_entry` | Decision S07-D8; 10.4.1 L13025-13026 leaves the order undefined. A value that deletes the entry keeps the write, for an array member, a record built from the element it replaces, deeper keys and packed records; selectors run once; a member array write reaches a copied queue element. Matches industry-standard behaviour. |
| `subroutine_container_waits` | §§9.4.2, 9.4.3. `wait` and `@` on containers of formals, automatic locals and class properties wake when the element, size or property changes. Matches industry-standard behaviour. |
| `nested_associative_handles` | §7.8; §8.5. Handles held in a nested associative array stay reachable through overwrites and shared elements; a subroutine called by the value of an element write sees the array it writes (`put`). Matches industry-standard behaviour. |
| `nested_associative_selectors` | §11.3.5 L14434-14435 (quoted under `call_container_operands`). A selector that calls a function runs once per evaluation of the select, and not at all in a skipped operand: `aa.exists("z") && aa[nm()].exists(1)` leaves `n` at 0. Matches industry-standard behaviour. |

### Clause quotes for `nested_element_methods`

- §7.4.5, `SystemVerilog-1800-2009.txt` L8122: "A multidimensional array is an array of arrays."
- §7.8, L8587: "Associative arrays do not have any storage allocated until it is used, and the index expression"
- §7.8.6, L8722-8723: "If an invalid index (i.e., 4-state expression has X’s) is used during a read operation or an attempt is made to / read a nonexistent entry, then a warning shall be issued; and the default initial value for the array type shall"
- §7.10.2.6, L9137: "The push_front() method inserts the given element at the front of the queue."
- §7.10.2.7, L9145: "The push_back() method inserts the given element at the end of the queue."
- §7.10.5, L9215-9217: "Operations on bounded queues shall behave exactly as if the queue were unbounded except that if, after any / operation that writes to a bounded queue variable, that variable has any elements beyond its bound, then all / such out-of-bounds elements shall be discarded and a warning shall be issued."
